Iqmal used MobileNetV2 in two projects: 

* **Food Image Classification (Dec 2025)**: a Streamlit application that uses a fine-tuned MobileNetV2 model to classify food images into 6 categories with 95% accuracy.
* **CNN Deep Learning Portable Dental Caries Detection (Jul 2023)**: an award-winning portable dental caries detection system using deep learning, where MobileNetV2 was used to achieve 80% detection accuracy.

evidence.path: Projects > Food image classification (Dec 2025) > Results and limitations
evidence.text: The final MobileNetV2 model classified 95 of the 100 validation images correctly (95%). This is a validation figure, not an independent test result: the same 100 images were used while choosing the model, and there is no separate untouched test set. The app always picks one of the six classes, even for photos of other foods, so an "unsupported image" option is a planned improvement. The public repository is a fork of another repository, so not every file in it was written by Iqmal.

evidence.path: Projects > Food image classification (Dec 2025) > Model and training
evidence.text: The final model is MobileNetV2 pretrained on ImageNet, with its classifier replaced by a six-class output layer (about 2.2 million parameters). It is fine-tuned with PyTorch using transfer learning and data augmentation: random horizontal flips, rotation of up to 15 degrees and colour jitter, with ImageNet normalisation. MobileNetV2 was chosen because its depthwise-separable convolutions make it light enough for fast inference on an ordinary CPU.

evidence.path: Projects > Portable dental image analysis app (final-year project, Jul 2023) > Mobile architecture
evidence.text: The Android app is written in Java. A USB endoscope connects to the phone as a UVC camera through the AndroidUSBCamera library (version 2.3.4). The trained MobileNetV2 model runs on the phone with PyTorch Mobile (version 1.12.1), so the image never leaves the device. The user captures an image, the app runs the model, and the predicted class is shown on screen.

evidence.text: For his final-year project at IIUM, Iqmal built a portable dental image-analysis application using a CNN (MobileNetV2). It analyses images from a small endoscopic camera on an Android phone, with no computer or cloud connection needed. The project reported 80% accuracy, was validated together with dental professionals, and won Best Overall Final Year Project in the Department of Mechatronics.

results.question: How does the scanner login stop people from just typing a password?

body.response:
**Secure Login Mechanism**: Iqmal designed the scanner login system to prevent unauthorized manual entry by implementing an **automatic login-window detection**. This feature detects when the login window is displayed and **locks keyboard input**, preventing users from typing a password manually. 

**Biometric Match Required**: After a successful **biometric match** (either fingerprint or facial recognition), the system **auto-fills credentials**, allowing authorized users to access the system securely. This ensures that only authorized individuals can gain access to the system, reducing the risk of unauthorized access.

evidence.path: Projects > Biometric login system for vision scanners (IQMETRIC, Jun 2026) > What it does
evidence.text: IQMETRIC is a multi-modal biometric login system for production vision scanners, built at NXP. It combines fingerprint and facial recognition so that a person must prove who they are before the scanner's login is unlocked. evidence.text: The application automatically detects the scanner's login window, locks keyboard input, and fills in credentials only after a successful biometric match, which prevents unauthorised manual entry.
